name: GoodWood Nola
old_description: Established in 2014 and rooted in New Orleans, GoodWood Nola is a family-owned design and build firm renowned for its dedication to crafting custom furniture and fabrication. Our mission is to sustainably produce high-quality work, shaping beautiful, timeless pieces that embody the essence of craftsmanship and design excellence. Celebrated for our commitment to best practices, we have earned accolades from industry leaders, affirming our role as a benchmark for quality and sustainability in the creative world. At GoodWood, we are not just building furniture; we are crafting spaces for life’s moments, driven by a passion for design, community, and the environment.
about:
GoodWood Nola, founded in 2014 in New Orleans, Louisiana, is a family-owned design and build firm. The company was established by co-founders Jordan Gurren Rose and Maggie Rose, who serve as owners, along with former co-founder Mike Dalle-Molle. Rooted in the city’s creative culture, the firm began with a focus on custom furniture and architectural fabrication.

The company operates as a fully licensed and insured specialty contractor, producing custom furniture, architectural elements, and precision parts for both commercial and residential clients. Its capabilities include CNC milling, engraving, signage, custom lighting, and product development, supported by a full-time team of local builders and designers. Materials span wood, steel, brass, aluminum, concrete, acrylic, solid surfaces, and plaster. Projects move through a three-step process: discovery, design, and fabrication.

GoodWood serves hospitality venues such as restaurants, bars, coffee shops, and hotels, as well as retail stores, salons, corporate offices, and private residences. Notable projects include build-outs for Paris Parker Carondolet, Longway Tavern, Capulet, Brass Kitchen, Walnut Kitchen, Zasu, and the Southern Rep Theater.

The firm emphasizes a human-centered, collaborative approach, positioning each project as an investment in relationship rather than mere transaction. Its stated mission is to sustainably produce high-quality, timeless pieces, a commitment that has earned recognition from industry peers.

name: Green Bay Packaging Inc - Valley Packaging Division
old_description: Valley Packaging Division takes pride in being a leading manufacturer of high-quality corrugated packaging. Our team of dedicated professionals is committed to delivering exceptional products and services to our valued customers across Tennessee, Alabama, Georgia, Mississippi, and Kentucky.
about:
Valley Packaging Division operates in Pulaski, Tennessee, as part of Green Bay Packaging, a family-owned company. The division serves customers across Tennessee, Alabama, Georgia, Mississippi, and Kentucky.

The division manufactures corrugated packaging using an in-house corrugator and high-speed automated equipment, including a flexo folder gluer, a 3-color flat die cutter, and a rotary die cutter. It produces 4-color direct-print boxes, shipping and labeled boxes, pre-print, assembled partitions, corrugated skids, auto-bottom boxes, pre-glued trays, and plastic corrugated products, along with non-corrugated supplies such as bubble wrap, tape, honeycomb, and corner board. Packaging engineers collaborate on custom designs using B, C, E, and BC double-wall flutes.

Primary markets include food, beverage, health, and beauty packaging, where BRCGS certification ensures food-safe standards, and the Sustainable Forestry Initiative (SFI) certification covers responsible fiber sourcing. The division also fulfills general packaging and fulfillment needs for regional businesses.

Green Bay Packaging emphasizes integrated mill operations that produce both recycled and virgin fiber materials, positioning the division as a sustainable supplier. A dedicated truck fleet provides just-in-time delivery, and the family-owned culture promotes career growth for employees.

name: Green Hills Foods
old_description: Green Hills Foods is a family-owned foodservice distributor, servicing Arkansas and the southern region of the United States since 1979. We specialize in delivering food and food-related products to our restaurant partners and emphasize building long-lasting relationships with our customers and suppliers.
about:
Green Hills Foods, a family-owned foodservice distributor, has operated from Springdale, Arkansas since 1979. Founded as a regional supplier to local restaurants, the company has grown into a multi-state operation serving customers across Arkansas, Texas, Oklahoma, Missouri, Alabama, Georgia, Indiana, Colorado, Kentucky, Kansas, Tennessee, Mississippi, Louisiana, and Illinois.

The distributor provides full-line foodservice distribution, supplying fresh produce, dry goods, seafood, meats, poultry, dairy, and disposable products to independent grocers, chain supermarkets, foodservice distributors, food manufacturers, and club stores. Its route delivery network services restaurants, markets, and wholesalers throughout its coverage area, with a focus on consistent product availability.

Green Hills Foods is recognized as the supplier for the Mexican restaurant industry in Arkansas and surrounding states. Its customer base includes independent and chain restaurants, institutional foodservice operators, and retail grocery outlets across the region, with particular strength in Mexican cuisine ingredients.

The company emphasizes building long-lasting relationships with both customers and suppliers, aiming to deliver quality inspected products at fair prices through an honest, trust-focused approach that has sustained its growth for over four decades.

name: Green Ridge Solar
old_description: Green Ridge is a local solar company that was born and raised in Oregon by two best friends, Alex and Brian. They saw a need for a legitimate and reputable solar company that served Oregon and Washington with integrity. Even today, they are still unafraid to get their hands dirty in the field with their install crew.
about:
Born and raised in Oregon, they recognized a need for a legitimate, reputable solar company that could serve both Oregon and Washington with integrity. From the start, the founders have remained hands‑on, working alongside their installation crews in the field.

The company designs and installs solar photovoltaic systems, battery storage, and EV chargers for residential, commercial, and municipal customers. Its services include custom system design, free consultation, professional installation, mobile monitoring setup, and ongoing maintenance such as panel cleaning, repair, and removal/reinstallation for roof work. Green Ridge Solar partners with SolarEdge for inverters and monitoring and with FranklinWH for battery storage, and backs every installation with a 25‑year workmanship warranty.

Customers range from homeowners seeking lower bills and backup power to farms, nonprofits, and government agencies. Notable projects include a 31.68 kW rooftop system for the Marion County Evidence Building in Salem, a ground‑mount array with four batteries for a Bend family, a horse‑farm installation in Brush Prairie, Washington, and a third‑party‑ownership solar install in Madras, Oregon. The company also services systems originally installed by other providers.

Green Ridge Solar differentiates itself through a zero‑pressure consultation model, deep local knowledge of Pacific Northwest permitting and incentives, and a dedicated service contact—known as 'Sam, the Service Savior'—who coordinates rapid response to any system issue. The founders started the business to provide a trustworthy, community‑focused alternative in a market they felt lacked integrity.

name: Griffin Foods
old_description: Griffin Food Company specializes in the production and packaging of liquid and emulsified semi-solid based food products. While our primary expertise is table syrups and mustards, our capabilities extend well beyond those categories. We offer multiple product sizes including retail packs, food service, and industrial.
about:
Griffin Foods is headquartered in Muskogee, Oklahoma, where it was founded in 1908 by brothers John T. and Charles M. Griffin. The company began as the Griffin Grocery Company in McAlester before moving to Muskogee in 1923, when John Griffin built a three-story facility housing administration, warehousing, and processing. Now a fourth-generation, family-owned and minority-owned business, it operates under the Griffin Holding Company alongside Griffin Communications.

The company specializes in manufacturing and packaging liquid and emulsified semi-solid food products, with core lines in table syrups, mustards, molasses, imitation vanilla, and corn syrups. Through its 2006 acquisition of House of Webster in Rogers, Arkansas, Griffin added gourmet jams, jellies, preserves, fruit butters, relishes, salsas, barbecue sauces, salad dressings, and pickled products. It offers co-packing and private-label services, formulating new products or running customer formulas, and packages in retail, foodservice, and industrial sizes. The Muskogee facility serves distribution across the continental U.S., Mexico, and Europe; by 2000 the company employed roughly 100 people and recorded several million dollars in annual sales.

Griffin supplies food manufacturers, foodservice distributors, and retail grocery chains, with its branded products stocked in most Oklahoma-area supermarkets. Major customers receive branded, private-label, and co-packed items, and the company sells direct by the case.

Griffin differentiates itself through food-safety certifications—SQF Food Safety Code for Food Manufacturing and Kosher Parve certification from the Orthodox Union—and a commitment to allergen-free production (no Big 8 allergens). The company emphasizes quick response, high-grade ingredients, and a track record of customer-service awards.

name: Grote Company
old_description: Since we were founded in 1972 by Jim Grote, we've been a family-owned and operated manufacturer known for exceptional customer service, unparalleled craftsmanship, dependability, and quality. While we continue to innovate and adapt to ever-changing trends and technologies, one thing has and will never change: our personal touch and a people-first approach.
about:
Grote Company is a family-owned manufacturer of industrial food slicing and assembly equipment based in Columbus, Ohio. Founded in 1972 by Jim Grote, the company began as a specialist in food processing machinery and has remained under family ownership for over five decades.

The company designs and builds three primary equipment lines: pizza topping lines that automate sauce depositing, pepperoni slicing, and cheese or IQF ingredient application; sandwich assembly lines that combine fixed equipment and robotics for depositing, slicing, assembling, aligning, and cutting; and a range of food slicers from multi-purpose offline models to high-speed multi-lane industrial units. Beyond hardware, Grote provides parts and blade ordering, training, equipment health assessments, field service, reconditioning, and replacement support, and operates demo facilities for customer product testing.

Grote serves food processors worldwide, including frozen pizza manufacturers, sandwich producers, meat processors slicing pepperoni and other proteins, jerky makers such as Las Vegas Jerky's, and bakery operations. Reference customers cited include Kunzler & Company and Martel Foods, which automated sandwich lidding with Grote robotics.

The company emphasizes an enduring commitment to service, citing durable equipment built to last, 50 years of application-specific expertise, and a partnership model that supports customers through every project phase. This people-first approach, rooted in the founder's original vision, remains the stated differentiator.

name: Growatt USA
old_description: Growatt USA specializes in solar inverter and energy storage solutions. Provides on-grid photovoltaic inverters, battery storage systems, EV chargers and monitoring equipment for residential and commercial solar projects.
about:
Growatt USA operates from Santa Ana, California, as the American subsidiary of a global renewable energy company founded in 2011 by David Ding and a group of photovoltaic industry pioneers in Shenzhen, China. The U.S. entity was established in 2013 to support the company's expanding footprint in the Americas.

The company designs and manufactures a broad portfolio of solar inverters ranging from 0.75 kW to 253 kW, lithium-ion battery storage systems for residential and commercial use, EV chargers (3–22 kW AC and 20/40 kW DC), and cloud-based monitoring hardware and software. Production is centered at an advanced manufacturing plant in Huizhou, China, which began operation in 2021. Globally, the organization employs over 1,000 people and reports more than 6 million end users connected to its cloud platform across 190-plus countries.

Growatt's solutions target residential, commercial, utility-scale, and transportation sectors. Its customer base includes solar installers, engineering-procurement-construction (EPC) firms, distributors, and end-users. The company works with thousands of local partners to distribute products such as the WIT series commercial inverters, APX high-voltage batteries, and the THOR smart EV charger, and it provides training programs for installers and EPCs.

The founder's stated vision is to build the world's largest intelligent sustainable energy ecosystem, with a mission to enable everyone to benefit from sustainable energy. The company emphasizes integrated "solar, storage, and EV charging" solutions managed through a smart energy platform that uses big data, AI, and IoT for generation and consumption prediction.

name: Gruenewald Manufacturing Co
old_description: Gruenewald Manufacturing Company has consistently set the standard for quality whipped cream equipment since 1952. Increase customer loyalty with signature toppings, as you are in full control of your choice of ingredients.
about:
Gruenewald Manufacturing Company, Inc. was founded in 1952 in Danvers, Massachusetts. The company began as a manufacturer of whipped cream equipment and has remained in continuous operation for over seven decades. The name Gruenewald, German for "green forest," reflects a long-standing emphasis on environmentally conscious production.

The company designs and builds whipped cream dispensers and related equipment for commercial food service operations. All products are manufactured in the United States, though the company does not disclose facility size, headcount, or annual production volumes. Its equipment is engineered to deliver consistent portion control and to accommodate a variety of cream types and flavorings.

Gruenewald serves the food service industry, supplying restaurants, cafes, bakeries, and other establishments that serve fresh whipped cream. The company emphasizes that its equipment allows operators to control ingredients and create signature toppings, which it says drives customer loyalty.

Gruenewald positions itself as the oldest U.S. manufacturer of whipped cream equipment. It highlights that its machines eliminate millions of pounds of landfill waste each year and reduce whipped cream costs by 50 to 75 percent, framing its products as both economically and environmentally advantageous.

name: Gulfstream Steel & Supply
old_description: Since 1990, Gulfstream Steel has been a dependable source of metal materials and services. Beyond just an extensive inventory, a wide network of material sources, and local delivery, Gulfstream is pleased to provide many value added services. Whether you need various metals, fabrication, machining, coatings, fasteners, pipe fittings, manufacturing or construction projects, we are ready to help. Gulfstream Steel is among the trusted
about:
Gulfstream Steel & Supply was founded in 1990 in Holly Ridge, North Carolina, as a locally owned and operated metals service center. The company began as a dependable source of metal materials and services for the eastern North Carolina region.

The company maintains an extensive inventory of carbon steel, stainless steel, aluminum, galvanized steel, and PVC pipe and fittings, and provides a range of value‑added processing services. Its capabilities include structural sawing, mitre and CNC cutting, plate burning and beveling up to 14‑inch thickness, CNC machining on HAAS VF9 and VF4 mills and a Quickmill gantry center, sheet and coil shearing, forming, and punching, as well as pipe and tube cutting, drilling, and slotting. An on‑site blast shop prepares surfaces with black beauty and steel shot media, and a dedicated hose shop assembles custom hydraulic and pneumatic hose assemblies. Gulfstream also operates a fleet of 24‑foot Freightliners, a 28‑foot tandem‑axle International, and a 53‑foot Volvo for delivery across southeastern North Carolina.

Gulfstream serves industrial, agricultural, manufacturing, MRO, and construction customers, with a particular focus on U.S. military installations, law‑enforcement agencies, first‑responder units, and K‑9 training facilities. The company has worked with prime vendors such as Darley Defense on training‑solution projects.

The business emphasizes local hiring, including veterans, and promotes next‑day delivery on most stock items with free local delivery on orders over $500. Its differentiation rests on a large regional inventory, in‑house processing equipment, and a commitment to coastal‑environment durability through quality control and corrosion‑resistant coatings.

name: Gus Willy Apparel
old_description: Our professional grade embroidery machines support 21 work stations.  The Gus Willy embroidery team has over 50 years experience and can put your logo on anything from polos, caps, pullovers and more.  We can even make your design pop with our 3D embroidery capabilities.
about:
Gus Willy Apparel was founded in 2017 in Metairie, Louisiana, by Craig Leaumont, who named the business after his third child, Gustave William Leaumont, known as Gus Willy. The company began as a custom apparel operation focused on screen printing and embroidery for teams and corporate clients.

Today the shop runs two automatic and four manual screen‑print presses alongside professional‑grade embroidery machines with 21 work stations, including 3D embroidery capability. An in‑house graphic design team prepares artwork for both decoration methods. Beyond apparel, the company supplies promotional items such as pens, koozies, water bottles, and custom etched tumblers, and has expanded into a full‑line safety distributor offering ANSI‑compliant high‑visibility vests, jackets, hard hats, helmets, gloves, and other job‑site essentials. Orders range from small crew outfitting to workforces of several hundred.

The customer base spans construction, manufacturing, utilities, oil and gas, youth sports leagues, and corporate accounts across the southeastern United States.

Leaumont started the venture to honor his son, who was diagnosed with non‑verbal autism in 2013, and the business emphasizes a one‑stop shop for apparel and safety, fast turnaround, durable materials, and local, responsive service.
